source_caption:
To convincingly portray the younger version of Harrison Ford’s character, William Jones, the production team bypassed traditional Hollywood casting channels and discovered actor Anthony Ingruber entirely through YouTube. Ingruber had built a modest online following by posting amateur videos of himself performing uncannily accurate impressions of a young Harrison Ford. When director Lee Toland Krieger saw the footage, he was struck not only by Ingruber’s spot-on vocal cadence and signature lopsided smirk, but by his genuine physical resemblance to Ford during his late-1970s Star Wars era. Ford himself was reportedly stunned by the casting, which allowed the filmmakers to seamlessly execute the emotionally charged flashback sequences practically, without relying on expensive and often jarring digital de-aging technology.

The Age of Adaline (2015), directed by Lee Toland Krieger, starring Blake Lively, Michiel Huisman, Harrison Ford, Ellen Burstyn. After a miraculous accident involving freezing waters and a lightning strike in 1937, a young woman ceases to age, forcing her to live a solitary, guarded existence on the run for eight decades until a chance encounter threatens to expose her long-held secret.

source_details.synopsis: The Age of Adaline is a 2015 American romantic fantasy film directed by Lee Toland Krieger and written by J. Mills Goodloe and Salvador Paskowitz. The film stars Blake Lively as Adaline, with Michiel Huisman, Harrison Ford, Kathy Baker, Amanda Crew, and Ellen Burstyn. Narrated by Hugh Ross, the story follows Adaline Bowman, a young woman who stops aging following an accident at the age of twenty-nine. The film was produced by Sidney Kimmel Entertainment and Lakeshore Entertainment. Principal photography took place in Vancouver from March 5 to May 5, 2014.
